title: Ambiguous selector resolution and migration plan for model version selectors
creator: Ava Moreno
description: We need a clear, unambiguous resolution semantics for model selectors (tag, semver ranges, exact semver, commit hashes) surfaced in the Redwood REST API and SDKs, and a migration plan for existing customers who relied on loosely-defined 'latest' behavior. This ticket defines precedence rules, SDK preflight validation options, fallback behaviors, performance-profile binding rules, telemetry events, and a recommended migration path (including tooling) to minimize regressions when models are updated or republished.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic precedence order is documented and reviewed by API/SDK and Runtime teams.
SDKs implement a new resolution client that supports 'strict' and 'lenient' modes with documented behavior for cache, preflight resolution, and fallback.
Runtime emits telemetry events model.resolve_attempt, model.resolve_result, model.resolve_fallback with schema documented in README.
Migration CLI prototype exists to scan customer configs and suggest concrete selector replacements (e.g., tag -> semver or commit hash) with a dry-run report.
Backward compatible default remains 'lenient' to avoid mass customer breakage; strict mode opt-in must be available in SDK and server-side per-route configs.
implementation_notes: Selector types supported: tag:<name>, semver:<range> (npm-style ranges allowed), semver-exact:<x.y.z>, commit:<sha256>. Example API field 'model_selector' now accepts objects or strings; SDKs normalize to a canonical internal string 'type:value' (e.g., 'tag:stable', 'semver:^1.2.0', 'commit:fa3b...').

Precedence (highest -> lowest): 1) explicit commit (commit:sha) 2) exact semver (semver-exact:1.2.3) 3) semver range (semver:^1.2.0) with deterministic tie-breaker by release timestamp 4) explicit tag (tag:canary, tag:stable) 5) channel alias 'latest' which resolves to a stable tag with a visibility window. This precedence must be implemented in both SDK and runtime resolver to ensure identical behavior.

Stability window for tags: tags have optional 'stability_window' metadata (days). Tag -> release mapping older than stability_window should emit a deprecation warning and a 'stale_tag' resolution flag in telemetry.

Fallback rules: when resolution fails, behavior depends on SDK mode: 'lenient' will fallback to the most recent compatible release according to compatibility matrix (major version match and quantization/variant fingerprint), 'strict' will return a 4xx error to the caller. Runtime global policy can override SDK with 'server_fallback: allow|deny'.

Performance profile binding: performance profiles are attached to model artifacts (release metadata). Resolution returns both resolved_model_ref and performance_profile_id. If client requested a variant (e.g., 'quantized=avx2'), the resolver will select the nearest performance_profile variant by feature flags; if none available, mark 'profile_fallback' and include suggested profile in response metadata.

SDK preflight resolution: SDKs should provide a 'resolve_preflight' API that attempts resolution using local cache and a single network roundtrip. Preflight supports timeout and can return a 'soft-fail' token allowing request to proceed with last-known-good model_ref. This enables low-latency clients to proceed while background reconciliation occurs.
Client validation: SDKs must validate selector syntax locally. Invalid selector strings should raise a client error before network call. Examples added to SDK docs and linters.
Audit and traceability: each resolution includes resolver_path (string) and origin (api|sdk-cache|runtime-cache). This appears in request trace logs for post-mortem and incident analysis.

Compatibility heuristics: maintain a small 'compatibility matrix' per model family that indicates safe-major/minor upgrade boundaries for automatic fallback resolution. This matrix is part of model manifest authored at onboarding time.

Migration tooling: a CLI 'redwood-pin-migrate' will scan repositories (YAML/JSON config, environment variables), detect loose selectors (e.g., 'latest', bare tags), and produce PR-ready suggestions with pinned semver or commit pins plus rationale and risk score.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Publish spec and RFC to internal docs; get sign-off from Runtime, SDK, Console, and Security teams.
Week 2: Implement resolver library in runtime and a mirrored resolver shim in SDKs (JS/Python) behind a feature flag.
Week 3: Release SDKs in minor with opt-in 'strict' mode and preflight API; expose telemetry schema in observability docs.
Week 4: Run migration CLI on a subset of customers (opt-in) and produce migration reports; iterate on messaging to Console for guidance.
Week 5: Flip default server-side resolution to enforcement for new routes only; monitor error rate and fallback metrics for two weeks; then evaluate wider rollout.
migration_tasks: Build CLI scanner binary and repo integrator (dry-run only for initial release).
Add a console UI page that shows 'pinning health' per project and suggests selectors to pin with one-click PR generation.
Create linter rule for infra-as-code specs to warn about 'latest' and bare tags during CI.
Coordinate with Docs to publish migration guide and example patterns per common runtime (node, python, go).
